question: What will the September 2026 Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey current general activity index read?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: the month-after prints following an extremely elevated MBOS current-activity reading. Identifiable instances give next-month values of 29.6 (Mar-17 after 41.4), 33.7 (May-21 after 48.8), 17.1 (Dec-21 after 44.0), 18.1 initial print (Feb-25 after 44.3 initial), 47.4 (Aug-26 after 41.4) — median ~30, mean change ~-15. A standard AR(1) view (series mean ~+9, monthly persistence ~0.75-0.8) puts September nearer 38. I split toward 34. Upward pull: the surge is corroborated, not noise — ISM manufacturing in its 8th straight expansion month at 54.6, MBOS employment index 27.9 (highest since Apr-22), future activity 73.6 (highest since Aug-83), reshoring capex intentions strong, August payrolls 3x consensus. Downward pull: August's headline diverged ABOVE its own internals (new orders 37.0->30.1, shipments 33.7->27.7, prices paid 53.9->40.9), ISM itself edged down from 55.6 with new orders off 3 points, and a diffusion index measuring month-over-month change requires continued acceleration off an already-raised base — no two consecutive 45+ prints appear anywhere in the 2015-2026 span. The Sept 15-16 FOMC (market-implied ~60% odds of a HIKE as of Sep 4) falls in the tail of the collection window. Left-skewed: downside has more room (May-26 printed -0.4 immediately after 26.7) while the upside runs into a near-record ceiling. Escapes: 3% above 60 would require an all-time-high-region print, plausible only if the two-month beat streak extends a third time; 1% below -10 needs a ~57-point one-month collapse, which only COVID-scale shocks have produced.
calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: Resolves off the INITIALLY PUBLISHED seasonally adjusted 'current general activity' diffusion index for the September 2026 reference month, in the Philadelphia Fed MBOS release scheduled 2026-09-17 ~08:30 ET — NOT off the later-revised FRED series (GACDFSA066MSFRBPHI), and NOT off any component index (new orders, shipments, employment) or the 'future general activity' index. Revisions after first print are ignored. Vintage matters: January 2025 printed 44.3 initially but stands at 32.9 in the current FRED revised series; July-2026 (41.4) and August-2026 (47.4) currently match across vintages.

EVENT WINDOW: The September reference month runs 2026-09-01 -> 2026-09-30 per the criteria, but the datum is generated by the survey collection window inside it. The August release states its responses were collected 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-17, implying a September collection window of roughly 2026-09-08 to 2026-09-15 (the Philly Fed does not publish collection dates in advance). As of Now = 2026-09-07T10:08Z, 0% of that collection window has elapsed; no September survey response has yet been recorded.

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: If nothing changes and the index simply repeats August, the print is 47.4. If it reverts to the series' own long-run central tendency, the print is near +9.

EVIDENCE — LEVELS AND HISTORY
- Aug-2026 current general activity: 47.4, up from 41.4 in July; described in the release as the highest reading since April 2021. 56.9% of firms reported increases, 9.6% decreases, ~29% no change. (Philadelphia Fed MBOS August 2026 report, released 2026-08-20.)
- Aug-2026 components moved the OTHER way from the headline: new orders 37.0 -> 30.1; shipments 33.7 -> 27.7; prices paid 53.9 -> 40.9. Employment rose 10.0 -> 27.9 (highest since April 2022). (Same release.)
- Future general activity index: 73.6, up ~39 points, described in the release as the highest since August 1983; ~75% of firms expect increases over the next six months. (Same release.)
- 2026 monthly path (FRED revised, GACDFSA066MSFRBPHI): Jan 12.6, Feb 16.3, Mar 18.1, Apr 26.7, May -0.4, Jun 10.3, Jul 41.4, Aug 47.4.
- 2025 monthly path (FRED revised): Jan 32.9, Feb 13.4, Mar 10.2, Apr -12.9, May -0.7, Jun -1.4, Jul 11.4, Aug 0.7, Sep 19.5, Oct -10.1, Nov 0.6, Dec -8.8. Initial prints for several of these months differed materially (Jan-25 initial 44.3, Apr-25 initial -26.4, Sep-25 initial 23.2, Oct-25 initial -12.8) per the mql5 economic calendar actual-vs-forecast log.
- Street consensus has been well below the actual for three consecutive months: Jun-26 actual 10.3 vs 3.0 expected; Jul-26 actual 41.4 vs 10.3 expected (Investing Live and mql5 record ~13.0 at some vendors); Aug-26 actual 47.4 vs 13.7 (mql5) / ~25.0 (Trading Economics) expected. No street consensus for the September print was published on any calendar I checked as of 2026-09-07.

BASE RATES, WITH THE CLASS EACH IS COMPUTED OVER
- Over ALL months 1968-2026 (FRED series): the index averages roughly +8 to +9 with a monthly standard deviation near 19-20, i.e. it is a mean-reverting, high-variance series.
- Over the 24 monthly CHANGES from Sep-2024 through Aug-2026 (FRED revised): sorted changes run -29.6, -27.1, -23.1, -19.5, -10.7, -9.4, -9.1, -8.1, -3.2, -0.7, +1.4, +1.8, +3.7, +6.0, +8.6, +9.2, +10.7, +10.7, +12.2, +12.8, +18.8, +21.4, +31.1, +42.5. Median +2.8; 10th-90th percentile band approximately -22 to +21 (width ~43).
- CONDITIONAL on the prior month printing >= 40 (five identifiable instances 2015-2026): the following month came in at 29.6 (Mar-17 after Feb-17's 41.4), 33.7 (May-21 after Apr-21's 48.8), 17.1 (Dec-21 after Nov-21's 44.0), 18.1 initial (Feb-25 after Jan-25's 44.3 initial), and 47.4 (Aug-26 after Jul-26's 41.4). Mean of those next-month levels ~29; mean change ~-15; the sample spans 17 to 47.
- CONDITIONAL on the prior month printing 30-40: Apr-21 came in at 48.8 after Mar-21's 37.9; Jun-21 at 32.0 after May-21's 33.7; Mar-20 at -19.4 after Feb-20's 36.4 (COVID regime break).
- FREQUENCY of extremes: over Jan-2015 to Aug-2026 (140 months, FRED revised) exactly two months printed >= 45 (Apr-2021 48.8 and Aug-2026 47.4), and no two consecutive months both printed >= 45. Three months printed <= -25 (Apr-2020, May-2020, Apr-2023), all inside COVID or the 2023 goods recession.

EVIDENCE — MACRO BACKDROP, BOTH DIRECTIONS
- ISM Manufacturing PMI, August 2026 (released 2026-09-01): 54.6%, down 1.0 point from July's 55.6%; 22nd consecutive month of overall-economy expansion, 8th consecutive month of manufacturing expansion. New Orders 53.7 (down 3.0 from 56.7); Production 58.3 (down 0.2); Employment 51.2 (down 1.6 from 52.8). Backlog and Imports indexes also lost ground. (ISM via PRNewswire / Industry Today, 2026-09-01.)
- August 2026 US non-farm payrolls came in roughly three times consensus with unemployment at 4.1% and prior months revised up; federal funds futures put ~60% odds on a Fed rate HIKE at the 2026-09-15/16 FOMC as of 2026-09-04. 2-year Treasury 4.379%, 10-year 4.783%. Bloomberg-surveyed economists expected August CPI at 3.4% y/y, core 2.4%. The August CPI and PPI releases land before the MBOS release. (Udn Money, 2026-09-05.)
- A September 2026 reshoring survey reported more OEMs reshoring than in 2025, with 63% planning US capital expenditure in 2026 or 2027, citing tariffs, geopolitical risk and customer proximity. (Floor Covering News, 2026-09.)
- Regional divergence: the Dallas Fed general business activity index for Texas manufacturing was around -0.2 in March 2026 with its outlook-uncertainty index at a post-April-2025 high, i.e. other districts were not sharing the Third District's strength earlier in the year. (Trading Economics.)
- The Third District universe is ~250 manufacturers in eastern Pennsylvania, southern New Jersey and Delaware — a small, concentrated panel, which is the mechanical reason this index is far noisier month-to-month than ISM.
- Mechanical note on the instrument: the headline is a stan
calls.reference_class: Philly Fed MBOS current general activity prints in the month immediately following a reading of 40 or higher (1968-2026; five verifiable modern instances), cross-checked against the unconditional AR(1) behaviour of the series 2015-2026

calls.reasoning: Status quo is 47.4 (Aug), the highest print since Apr 2021, reached after 41.4 in July. Prior from the named class: of the 21 months since 1968 with a print >=40, the following month fell a median 5.5 points (mean -6.2, SD 10.3), implying ~41.9. Two conditionals cut against each other: back-to-back >=40 prints (n=9, 1972-73 and 1983-84) reverted only -4.1 on average, but the five post-1990 >=40 prints reverted a median -14.2, and a simple AR(1) on 2015-2026 implies ~30. I land the median at 36, below the broad class and above the modern sub-class. Pulling down: Philly at 47.4 is a large outlier versus ISM 54.6 (down 1.0, new orders down 3.0) and Empire State 20.6; Philly's own new orders (30.1) and shipments (27.7) fell while the standalone headline question rose; the print beat a ~24.1 consensus by ~23 points, and a ~125-firm panel makes such a gap partly sampling noise that does not persist. Pulling up: future general activity 73.6 is the highest since Aug 1983, employment jumped to 27.9, and the macro backdrop is hot (payrolls ~3x consensus, ~60% odds on a September Fed HIKE). Tails are wide and left-skewed: no seasonally adjusted reading >=60 exists in 58 years (max 58.5, Mar 1973), so I price only 3% above the open upper bound; a drop below -10 needs a ~57-point one-month collapse, seen only in COVID, so 0.5%. Evidence is genuinely two-sided and no market prices this.

calls.reference_class: Months since 1968 in which the Philadelphia Fed MBOS seasonally adjusted current general activity index printed >= 40, and the value printed the immediately following month (n~21, FRED series GACDFSA066MSFRBPHI)

calls.reasoning: Base rate first: across all MBOS months since 1968 with current general activity >= 38, the mean following-month change is about -5.3, anchoring ~42 from August's 47.4; the five modern-era (post-2015, smaller respondent panel) instances averaged about -14, and mean reversion from a ~98th-percentile level is the dominant historical force. Against that, the regime looks genuine rather than a one-month spike: two consecutive 40s prints, future general activity at 73.6 (highest since 1983), employment at 27.9 (highest since April 2022), ISM manufacturing at 54.6 in its eighth expansion month, strong August payrolls, and a consensus that has undershot this index for four straight months (Jul 41.4 vs 13.0 expected; Aug 47.4 vs ~13.7-24 expected) - so I deliberately do not anchor on pre-2026 norms. The main mechanical drag is the diffusion base effect: the question asks about change versus the prior month, so holding ~47 net-increase for a third month requires accelerating growth, and August's own internals already diverged (new orders -7 to 30.1, shipments down to 27.7, ISM new orders -3.0). I therefore center at 36, below the all-history class anchor of ~42 but well above the pre-boom mean, with a left-skewed spread reflecting that big one-month retracements (-19 to -27) are the modal failure of high prints. No matching prediction market exists; the ISM and Fed Kalshi contracts are different instruments entirely.

calls.reference_class: Philadelphia Fed MBOS months with a seasonally adjusted current general activity index >= 38, 1968-2026 (n~21): the value printed the following month

calls.reasoning: Class anchor: months after a >=40 print fell a median ~5.5 pts since 1968, implying ~42 from August's 47.4; the five post-1990 instances reverted ~14, implying ~33. That gap is composition, not noise: pre-1990 >=40 prints came in multi-month booms, post-1990 ones were isolated spikes. September 2026 resembles the boom case (two straight 40+ prints, employment 27.9 highest since Apr-22, future activity 73.6 highest since Aug-83, ISM 54.6 in an 8th expansion month, payrolls ~3x consensus, consensus undershooting for 3-4 months), so I weight persistence more than the runs did. Offsetting: a ~125-return panel gives the diffusion index a ~6-pt sampling SD, so part of 47.4 is unrepeatable; August's internals diverged below the headline (new orders 37.0->30.1, shipments 33.7->27.7); and a change-diffusion index needs accelerating growth to hold 47 off a raised base, with no consecutive 45+ prints anywhere in 2015-2026. Median 37, left-skewed because retracements of -19 to -27 are the modal failure of high prints while the upside runs into a 58.5 all-time ceiling. No prediction market prices this instrument (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi checked by the runs; only ISM and FOMC contracts exist, different instrument and source), so no crowd anchor was available or used.
calls.reconciliation: Disputes were mostly vintage and sample-composition, not substance. The Run 2 vs Run 3 conflict over the modern post->=40 instance values (41.4->29.6 vs 43.3->32.8, etc.) is a FRED-revised vs Bank bos_dift.txt vintage artifact; with no web access I could not settle which vintage the initial-print class should use, and I let it stand because both give a modern next-month change of -12 to -14, so the conclusion is vintage-invariant. The broad-class (-5.5) vs modern-class (-14) gap I settled as composition rather than disagreement: the pre-1990 >=40 months clustered in the 1972-73 and 1983 booms, the post-1990 ones were isolated spikes, and the current setup (two consecutive 40+ prints, record future-activity, rising employment, national corroboration) matches the cluster case. That is the reason I sit at 37, above all three runs, rather than at their pool. The AR(1) persistence dispute (0.75-0.8 vs 0.5-0.6) could NOT be settled - neither run could run the regression - so I carried it as a 30-38 anchor range inside the dispersion rather than picking a side. The sampling-noise point (diffusion SD ~6 pts on ~125 returns, computed from the published 56.9/9.6 split) is the one hard fact that forces some reversion regardless of the macro story, and it caps how far up the persistence argument can take me. I adopt Run 3's reference class and a dispersion near Run 1/Run 3's (34), and the runs' unanimous 'no matching market' finding. No sources were retrieved on this run.
